title: Neural network detector finds bottom-of-sulcus dysplasia on MRI plus FDG-PET
summary: Bottom-of-sulcus dysplasia (BOSD) is often missed on MRI. Using the Multi-centre Epilepsy Lesion Detection group's machine-learning method with added FDG-PET features, neural network classifiers were trained on 54 patients with BOSD. On MRI+PET features, 87% of BOSDs were overlapped by one of the top five output clusters (69% top cluster) in training, 94% (88% top cluster) in 17 subsequently diagnosed patients from the same centre, and 75% (58% top cluster) in 12 published patients from another centre; MRI-only or PET-only training generally did worse. The test sets are small and the detector only suggests regions to scrutinize.
ai_technology: Neural network classifiers (MELD-based method plus FDG-PET features) detecting BOSD on MRI and PET
organization: Royal Children's Hospital; The University of Melbourne; Florey Institute of Neuroscience and Mental Health

evidence.tested: Neural network detection of bottom-of-sulcus dysplasia on MRI plus FDG-PET in 54 training patients, tested on 17 later same-centre patients and 12 published patients.
evidence.unknown: Performance in larger independent cohorts and effect on clinical decisions; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Neural networks trained on MRI and FDG-PET cortical features flag candidate dysplasia regions.
